what: Expected vs actual API responses for THIS app (acn-admin), covering Company, Press Release and Events — the admin-side counterpart to the public-site capture in the parent folder.
whyThisFolderExists: The four files one level up (../_index.json, ../company.json, ../press-release.json, ../events.json) were captured against the PUBLIC SITE's Next.js repo. That app has a different service layer (src/services/*), different interfaces and different mapping decisions, so its `expected` column describes code that does not exist here. Both apps talk to the same wire. These files re-run the same comparison against this repo's src/lib/api/*, so the two can be laid side by side and the API call unified.
probedFrom: local machine, direct curl against the live host — no /wire proxy, no IndexedDB cache, so these are true upstream responses.

hosts.api: https://development.acnnewswire.com  (the only host this app talks to — see src/lib/api/client.ts UPSTREAM_URL)
hosts.proxy: /wire — same-origin prefix, vite.config.ts in dev and vercel.json in deployment. Exists because the API's CORS is an allowlist, not a wildcard.
hosts.legacy: NOT USED by this app. The public site additionally calls https://www.acnnewswire.com/acnnewswireapi for enrichment; that host has been 503 since 2026-08-27. This repo has no dependency on it.

definitions.expected: The shape this repo codes against — the TypeScript interfaces in src/lib/api/types.ts, the parameter declarations in src/lib/api/endpoints.ts, and the documented assumptions in the surrounding comments.
definitions.actual: A verbatim live capture, with strings over 300 chars truncated and a marker appended. Credentials are redacted.
definitions.LIVE: The mismatch affects code that runs today.
definitions.LATENT: The endpoint is typed, exported and tested, but has no caller outside src/lib/api/map-article.test.ts. The mismatch bites on first use.

coverage: All 13 operations in the swagger document were probed. Every one answered.

files.shapeFidelity: 2 / 2 exact — every problem here is data, not shape

topFindings.finding: The API's sector ids are a different numbering from src/lib/sectors.ts. mapSector() resolves by id; only 7 of 22 sampled pairs agree, and 6 resolve to a DIFFERENT, REAL sector name.
topFindings.consequence: Wrong-but-plausible sector names are written into CompanyFull and cached. A blank field is visibly missing; a wrong sector name is not.
topFindings.actionable: FIXABLE HERE TODAY — match on `name` first in src/lib/api/map-company.ts. Name-matching resolves 18 of 22. map-article.ts already matches by name, so the two mappers currently disagree with each other.

topFindings.finding: GET /api/Companies and /api/Companies/{id} return plaintext `username` and `password` on unauthenticated endpoints.
topFindings.consequence: Worse here than on the public site: this app syncs ALL 9,606 companies, so a full sync writes 9,606 plaintext credential pairs into the browser's IndexedDB, where they persist across sessions.
topFindings.actionable: Backend must strip them from both DTOs. Until then this repo can stop mapping them, so they are at least never written to disk.

topFindings.finding: The Events list returns 7 upcoming events instead of 839 spanning 2007-2026, with compId null and companies[] empty on every row.
topFindings.consequence: No event can show its press releases or name its organiser, and only 7 event ids resolve at all. AE-RELEASES is healthy — there is simply no value to pass it.
topFindings.actionable: Backend-side. Confirm intent with the API team before changing code; the current code is correct-but-oversized, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.

topFindings.finding: GET /api/Articles/search is typed as `ApiArticleListItem[]` but returns a flat 34-key article × company × exchange JOIN row with no `companies[]` and no `images[]` at all.
topFindings.consequence: mapArticleListItem opens with `api.companies.map(...)`, so the first real call throws a TypeError. Nothing calls it today, which is the only reason this has not been seen.
topFindings.actionable: FIXABLE HERE — declare a separate ApiArticleSearchItem before anyone wires up search.

topFindings.finding: GET /api/Articles/by-company returns the full press-release shape, not ApiArticleFeedItem. `sectorName` is absent entirely; `language`, `sectors`, `bodyHtml` and four more fields are present and undeclared.
topFindings.consequence: mapArticleFeedItem would classify every company-feed release as unclassified while discarding a `language` that is on the wire. Three endpoints share one type but ship two shapes.
topFindings.actionable: FIXABLE HERE — type by-company off the press-release shape; keep ApiArticleFeedItem for homepage and by-industry.

topFindings.finding: On GET /api/Articles, `SecId` and `ArtType` are silently IGNORED (byte-identical results to an unfiltered call), and `Cid` is a source id, not a company id — Cid=82/574/9453 return [], Cid=2/3/4/5 each return a distinct set.
topFindings.consequence: Any list filter built on SecId or ArtType returns unfiltered data while appearing to work. Only HasThumbnail actually filters.
topFindings.actionable: Correct the parameter docs and do not expose SecId/ArtType as filters. Raise Cid with the API team — see AE-M4 for the same substitution on a second endpoint.

topFindings.finding: The press-release detail endpoint DOES return `language`. The code says it does not and threads the value in from the cached list row instead.
topFindings.consequence: A cold-cache article open — a direct URL, a cleared IndexedDB — loses the language and falls back to English, when the correct value was in the response all along.
topFindings.actionable: FIXABLE HERE TODAY — two lines, and it decouples loadArticleRecord from the list cache.

topFindings.finding: by-industry does not match `sector_name`. Of the 75 sector_names in lib/sectors.ts, only 4 return rows. What it matches is the coarse article `sectorName` set — Business, Healthcare, Technology, Industrial, Automotive — three of which are sector_TYPE values in the master list.
topFindings.consequence: An industry filter driven from the app's sector list comes back empty for 71 of 75 options.
topFindings.actionable: This is the third taxonomy in play. Needs one taxonomy agreed with the API team; see AC-M1 for the id half of the same problem.

topFindings.finding: `hasImage` was false on 100 / 100 consecutive list rows while 28 of them carried a non-empty images[]. `imageUrl` was null on 100 / 100.
topFindings.consequence: hasImage is not a usable signal. Notably the HasThumbnail QUERY parameter works correctly, so the server knows — it just does not say so in the field.
topFindings.actionable: FIXABLE HERE — branch on images.length, never on hasImage.

topFindings.finding: /api/Companies/{id}/details contributes nothing the main call does not already carry. Across 8 companies it returned only marketId "1", the six social links byte-identical to those on /api/Companies/{id}, and pos1Desc/pos2Desc "CEO" with no matching name.
topFindings.consequence: One of three requests per company editor load is redundant. The Company details tab and the address block have no data source at all — every address, telephone, email, established, listed and employees field was empty on all 8.
topFindings.actionable: Frontend can drop the call. But ask upstream first — it is the only endpoint that could ever carry an address.

crossCuttingThemes.theme: Three sector taxonomies, none of which agree
crossCuttingThemes.detail: (1) src/lib/sectors.ts — 75 sector_names under 9 sector_types, with its own ids. (2) The company endpoint's sectors[] — fine-grained names under a DIFFERENT id numbering (AC-M1). (3) The article endpoints' sectorName — a coarse 5-value set whose members are mostly sector_TYPEs in the master list (AP-M5). Meanwhile the press-release endpoint's sectors[] uses taxonomy (1)'s names correctly. Unifying the API call means picking one of these and stating the mapping to the other two.

The `Cid` parameter on /api/Articles and the `companyId` field on /api/Events/company/{id}/year/{year} both carry source ids (2 = ACN Newswire, 3 = JCN Newswire) rather than company ids. Two unrelated endpoints making the same substitution reads as a backend-wide naming problem, not two typos.

crossCuttingThemes.theme: Casing and end-of-list are per-endpoint, not per-API
crossCuttingThemes.detail: companyId vs companyID, logoFilename vs logoFileName, Page/Size vs pageNumber/pageSize — all already absorbed by this repo's types and mappers. Less well handled: end-of-list is [] on /api/Articles, 404 on /api/Articles/by-company, and Page is ignored entirely on /api/Articles/search. Error bodies come in three shapes (RFC9110 problem+json, {message}, {message, detail}).

crossCuttingThemes.theme: Shape fidelity is inverted between pages
crossCuttingThemes.detail: Company and Events declare their shapes exactly right and fail on DATA (empty details, null compId). Press Release declares two shapes materially wrong but the data is complete and healthy. The two pages need opposite kinds of work: Events needs the API team, Press Release needs a type pass in this repo.

unificationChecklist.purpose: What has to be agreed before one API client can serve both apps. Ordered by what blocks what.
askTheApiTeam: Is the Events 839 → 7 collapse intentional, and will compId / companies[] be repopulated? (AE-M1/M2/M3 — blocks every event feature in both apps.)
Strip username/password from the Companies DTO. (AC-M2 / C-M7 — security, both apps.)
Which sector taxonomy is authoritative, and what are the id mappings between the company sectors[] ids and the article sectorName set? (AC-M1 / AP-M5 — blocks any shared classification code.)
Is `Cid` on /api/Articles, and `companyId` on the event-releases feed, meant to be a source id? (AP-M4 / AE-M4.)
Are SecId and ArtType meant to filter? They are currently accepted and ignored. (AP-M4.)
Is /api/Companies/{id}/details empty because the dev DB is sparse, or because the DTO drops the fields? (AC-M3 — decides whether the call can be deleted.)
Is /api/Events/{id} on the fix list? (AE-M5 — unchanged for days.)
Is /api/Articles/search's ignored `Page` intentional? It returns a fixed 10-row window. (AP-M1.)
fixableInThisRepoNow: AC-M1 — resolve sectors by name in map-company.ts (one expression; align it with map-article.ts, which already does).
AP-M3 — add `language` to ApiPressRelease and read it in mapPressRelease (two lines).
AP-M1 — declare ApiArticleSearchItem before search gets a caller.
AP-M2 — split ApiArticleFeedItem so by-company is typed off the press-release shape.
AP-M6 — branch on images.length, not hasImage.
AC-M2 (partial) — stop mapping portal_username/portal_password so they never reach IndexedDB.
Comment corrections: AP-M8 (homepage is not empty), AE-M7 (the eventImage path is known), AC-M5 and AP-M-volume (record counts).
sharedShapesWorthExtracting: ApiArticleCompany — identical on press-release, by-company, homepage and events. One definition would serve both repos.
The language tag map (EN / JA / ZH-CN / ZH-TW / KO). This repo's LANGUAGE_BY_API_TAG covers every value observed across 113 sampled articles; the site has its own in src/lib/languages.ts.
